question: What has actually happened after an executive order was signed?
answer: Only 4 of the 509 orders on the record have any follow-through written up in the library's confirmed list of changes: 7 records on EO 14178, EO 14215, EO 14395, EO 14431. 3 deadlines set by EO 14395 have passed with no public record of the deliverables. For the other orders the library has no dated record of what happened next, which is not the same as nothing happening.

groups.label: EO 14178 · Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology
groups.note: Signed January 23, 2025, published January 31, 2025. State today: no revocation on record.

items.title: EO 14178 Working Group report published
items.sub: July 30, 2025 · Something the order asked for (section 4(c))
items.text: The President's Working Group publishes EO 14178's 180-day digital-assets report
kv: The White House published the Working Group's report and recommendations on July 30, 2025.

Publication satisfies the report-output clock; it is not a charter, statute, rule, issuer approval, operating stockpile account, stablecoin licence, CBDC termination receipt or proof that any recommendation was implemented.
EO 14178 had established the Working Group inside the National Economic Council and directed a 180-day regulatory and legislative report.
Being implemented, Operating, Paid or delivered, Effect observed
A named agency instrument, statutory enactment, account, custody record or operating action that identifies the report recommendation it carries forward.

groups.label: EO 14215 · Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies
groups.note: Signed February 18, 2025, published February 24, 2025. State today: no revocation on record.

items.title: Independent-regulator coordination overlay
items.sub: February 18, 2025 · Created by the order (section 1, 2); Created by the order (section 3, 4)
items.text: EO 14215 places independent-agency rules and management inside a presidential coordination overlay
kv: The signed order directs significant independent-agency regulatory actions through OIRA review and adds OMB performance, coordination and lawful apportionment controls while excluding Federal Reserve monetary policy.

The order creates direction and coordination duties; it does not transfer statutory authority, prove a particular rule was changed, place monetary policy under OIRA or establish that funds were withheld.
Independent regulators retained their statutory authorities without this executive-order-wide OIRA rule-review and OMB performance and apportionment overlay.
signature: 2025-02-18; publication: 2025-02-24; downstream operation: object-specific and unresolved
A named independent-agency rule review, performance action, lawful apportionment adjustment, judicial disposition or other record proving how the overlay changed an actual decision.

groups.label: EO 14395 · Establishing the Task Force To Eliminate Fraud
groups.note: Signed March 16, 2026, published March 19, 2026. State today: no revocation on record.

items.title: Fraud Task Force authority established
items.sub: March 16, 2026 · Created by the order (section 2, 3); Created by the order (section 4)
items.text: EO 14395 establishes the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and its timed control-output architecture
kv: The signed order establishes an EOP task force, names its member agencies and requires vulnerability descriptions, minimum controls and measurable implementation plans.
agency inventories due April 15, 2026; minimum controls due May 15, 2026; implementation plans due June 14, 2026
Task-force authority and coordination do not pause a named payment, decide eligibility, establish fraud, recover money or prove that the required deliverables were completed.
Federal benefit, payment, eligibility and enforcement owners operated without this EOP task force and its common 30-, 60- and 90-day output clocks.
Being implemented, Operating, Paid or delivered, Effect observed
A complete public deliverable set, named agency implementation record, attributable payment or eligibility action, or case-level result.

items.title: DOJ fraud operating architecture launched
items.sub: August 24, 2026 · Proof it is being carried out (section 3, 4)
items.text: DOJ codifies a National Fraud Enforcement Division and launches a multi-agency Fraud Detection Center under the task-force architecture
kv: A DOJ final rule made the National Fraud Enforcement Division effective and DOJ launched a prosecutor-led multi-agency National Fraud Detection Center to generate investigative leads.

Codified organization and launch establish implementation architecture; they do not publish the data agreements or matching logic, prove a Center-generated case, decide eligibility, stop a named payment or establish recovered dollars.
EO 14395 had created coordination and output duties without a public named cross-agency lead-fusion center or codified DOJ fraud division in this architecture.
Operating, Paid or delivered, Effect observed
final rule publication: 2026-08-18; division effective: 2026-08-24; center launch: 2026-08-24
Published agreements and controls, lead volume and disposition, or a first case explicitly traced from Center signal through owner decision, judgment and collected recovery.

items.title: Fraud Task Force deliverables gate
items.sub: September 14, 2026 · Still waiting on a record (section 4)
items.text: EO 14395's complete 30-, 60- and 90-day deliverable sets remain publicly unproved
kv: Related agency actions and White House rollups were public, but the research owner did not locate one complete public set of the required deliverables.
agency inventories due April 15, 2026 (past due, no record); minimum controls due May 15, 2026 (past due, no record); implementation plans due June 14, 2026 (past due, no record)
A bounded public non-finding is not proof that internal submissions were never made and does not negate separately proved agency or DOJ implementation.
The order required agency vulnerability descriptions, coordinated minimum controls and measurable implementation plans on matured clocks.
A complete public agency submission set, coordinated minimum-requirements instrument or measurable implementation-plan set.

groups.label: EO 14431 · Enhancing Program Integrity and Interagency Coordination in the Administration of the H-1B Nonimmigrant Visa Program
groups.note: Signed September 18, 2026, published September 23, 2026. State today: no revocation on record.

items.title: H-1B interagency integrity overlay
items.text: EO 14431 creates a six-agency H-1B integrity and review overlay
kv: The signed order directs six-agency consultation, sponsor-layoff consideration, a Wage and Hour review start gate and four-department delegation.
No downstream rule, guidance, review start, case decision, payment rail or observed effect is established.
Separate LCA, petition, visa and entry lanes operated without this directed cross-agency overlay.
signature or decision: 2026-09-18; filing: 2026-09-22 11:15 EDT; publication: scheduled 2026-09-23; implementation: 30-day WHD start gate
Downstream rule or guidance, documented WHD review start, first case action or observed result.

items.title: H-1B downstream implementation gate
items.sub: September 22, 2026 · Still waiting on a record (section 3(b), 3(c))
kv: No public downstream rule, guidance, fee rail, adjudication instruction or first enforcement receipt was established by the cutoff.
Checked public absence is not proof of inactivity or nonpublic instruction.
The signed order created implementation duties.
research cutoff: 2026-09-22 11:51:46 EDT; implementation gate: 30 days after 2026-09-18
Agency rule, guidance, review-start record or first attributable operating action.

uncertain: The confirmed list of changes is small on purpose: a record joins only with a named actor, a dated official record, a stage and a limit on what it proves. Other orders may have follow-through the library has read about but not written up.
A public non-finding (for example EO 14395's deliverables) does not prove the agencies never sent them internally.

EO 14431 set a 30-day start gate for the Wage and Hour review; counted from signing (September 18, 2026) that falls on October 18, 2026, which has passed with no recorded start. The master records the gate as text, not as a date.
